source.title: Generalization Matters: Loss Minima Flattening via Parameter Hybridization for Efficient Online Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Tianli Zhang; Mengqi Xue; Jiangtao Zhang; Hao-Fei Zhang; Yu Wang; Le-Chao Cheng; Jie Song; Ming-Li Song

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains models with parameter hybridization and reports held-out accuracy and qualitative loss-landscape comparisons. It does not test the specific interventions or measurements in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: Rows record reported test-accuracy results for the study’s own training method and selected comparisons, plus its noisy/limited-data results and ablation. Cited findings from prior work and landscape values visible only in figures are not recorded as numeric results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima improve generalization to design OKDPH and evaluates its performance. It tests none of V1–V8. Its PCA landscape visualizations do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, train–test gaps, or comparative rankings of generalization measures required by V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they present parameter hybridization as promoting flatter minima and more stable convergence, report better performance than compared OKD and flat-minima methods, and acknowledge that hybridization requires homogeneous students. The flatness evidence is qualitative and does not establish V7.
record.recipe_differences: The method trains multiple peer students with sampled convex combinations of their parameters, HWM supervision loss, and periodic parameter fusion; it is an online distillation and regularization recipe, not one of the listed original interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report sensitivity to the loss weights ω and β, fusion ratio γ, and fusion interval Δ; the tabulated accuracy varies with these settings (Table 4).

fits_no_version.finding: OKDPH reports higher test accuracy than the compared methods across the tabulated standard image-classification settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter hybridization with online distillation can improve single-model test accuracy in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: OKDPH reports higher accuracy than the compared OKD methods under noisy training images and random training-data subsampling; R15 and R16 require corrected values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: OKDPH can improve accuracy relative to tested OKD methods with noisy or limited training data.

fits_no_version.finding: Sequential ablations associate adding fusion and HWM classification loss with accuracy improvements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fusion and HWM classification loss contribute to OKDPH's performance in the tested configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1 and 4 qualitatively depict broader, flatter PCA-projected training-loss basins for OKDPH than for the compared training methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: OKDPH produces qualitatively flatter projected loss landscapes in the tested ResNet32 settings.

record.problems: The study reports top-1 test accuracy rather than train-test gaps. The landscape comparison is qualitative and shown in figures; other OKD baselines with extra modules or branches are omitted from that comparison because parameter quantities differ. Several stability-table results lack reported uncertainty; ImageNet table lacks uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 contains separate comparator results for each dataset and backbone; these were not all extracted because the 60-row cap prioritizes the study's own method results and condition changes. Table 3 additional comparator entries were not extracted. Table 4 hyperparameter sensitivity values were omitted because they are used to analyze settings and do not directly report the claim's named gap measure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training under matched architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout interventions, small-data dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps at comparable training loss, including rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of examples selected by label memorization compared with equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to claim versions. Their cannot_determine states indicate that these measurements cannot establish a named version, not that the reported accuracies are unreadable. No additional result in the supplied text warrants a verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label comparison against random-label training.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

tranche.reason: The study uses the flat-minima generalization premise to develop OKDPH and evaluates its own method. Its PCA landscapes and noisy or limited image-data experiments do not test V1–V8.
